column1: # WHAT JAVAC CANNOT START WITHOUT, on the way from JDK 21 to JDK 25.
# Short on purpose, and it used to be fifteen rows. The module gate compiles immediately
# after the bump and the hardens list is raised behind it, so a floor only matters here if
# a compile fails without it. Lombok does: it is an annotation processor running inside
# javac, an old one dies on TypeTags, and nothing in the bump phase raises it. Kotlin does
# above 21, and for a worse reason than crashing: 1.x silently falls back below the target,
# which the gate reads as an unraised bump and files against the repository.
# Everything else moved to hardens. Most of it was only ever needed for the TEST run, which
# happens at the repository gate, after that list has been raised.
# Every row is the head of a line and answers only for projects already on it: same major, same
# minor, lower patch. One artifact may hold several rows, one per line.
# group:artifact <tab> version <tab> any|maven|gradle <tab> other spellings, comma separated
# WHY THESE TOMCAT VERSIONS. Measured on this corpus, not read off a compatibility table:
# tomcat-embed-core 9.0.65 scores 22 CRITICAL+HIGH, 9.0.83 scores 19, 9.0.105 scores 14. Nothing in
# a Java bump ever looked at that. Tomcat moved because SPRING moved -- Boot 2.7.18 pins
# tomcat.version 9.0.83 -- so a project inherited whichever Tomcat its framework happened to carry,
# and 9.0.83 is the last patch of Boot 2.7's line rather than of Tomcat's. 10.1.55 is what Boot
# 3.5.16 pins, and the exact version trivy names as the fix for what the newest Tomcat 9 carries.
# The family moves in lockstep or the build breaks: tomcat-embed-core, -el and -websocket share a
# version by contract.
org.projectlombok:lombok
